function: Jointly learns task partitioning ratios (device, edge node, cloud) and uplink channel selection per IIoT device to minimize task completion latency in LEO satellite MEC (p. 8).
system: 5 LEO satellites with MEC servers, 50 IIoT devices, cloud server; OFDMA uplink, 10 channels of 1 MHz; antennas and frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 5, 11).
method: Deep recurrent Q-network (LSTM plus fully connected layers) per device; reinforcement learning with federated averaging of uploaded models at satellite edge nodes (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: LEO geometry, large-scale path loss plus small-scale fading with atmospheric attenuation, parameters in Table II adopted from [11]; no 3GPP model or measured data (pp. 5, 10-11).
test_conditions: Table II simulation has 50 devices; after training the model is deployed fixed and the number of terminals is varied, about 20 to 200 (pp. 11, 13).
baselines: Random partitioning, GA heuristic, DQN, and DRQN without federated learning (p. 12).
metrics: Average task completion latency (ms), reward and loss convergence, average partitioning ratios versus number of terminals (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Time complexity O(tau C) from layer widths of fully connected and LSTM layers; FedAvg aggregation O(N F) for N models of F parameters; no measured runtime (p. 10).
openness: none; no code or data link, parameters only in Tables II and III (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 5: "represents all time-varying small-scale fading components" (generic fading model, no standardized model named); p. 10: "The parameter values from [11] are adopted for consistency" (own simulator, no 3GPP or measured channel).
q2_support: p. 13: "Upon completing the training phase, the model is deployed on each agent" and "we manipulate the number of terminals in this experiment" (Figs. 13-14 vary terminals from about 20 to 200; Table II, p. 11, lists 50 devices).
q3_support: p. 12: "The second scheme, GA, utilizes a heuristic algorithm. The third scheme, DQN, deploys a DQN model in each agent." Non-learned: GA and Random; learned: standard DQN; compared on average latency (Figs. 12-14, p. 13). DRQN without FL is an ablation and is not counted.
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall time complexity of the DRQN algorithm is O(τ C)" (plus O(N F) for the federated averaging).
q5_support: p. 10: "The implementation of the federated DRQN algorithm is carried out using Python and PyTorch" (own simulator; no code or data link and no public channel dataset).
notes: Borderline above_phy: the main objective is MEC task partitioning, but the same agent also learns uplink channel selection, a resource allocation of a satellite link (p. 8), which the protocol counts as physical layer when learned jointly, so area 6 applies; reviewer to confirm. The FL is plain FedAvg of uploaded models (p. 10), not over the air, so area 7 does not apply. The title on page 1 matches the DOI.
